stem: Siddharth holds three transparent pieces close to a printed letter on a page: a convex lens, a concave lens, and a flat glass strip.

parts.text: Which claim about how the letter appears is correct?

options.text: Through the flat glass strip the letter looks the same size and shape.
Through the flat glass strip the letter always looks erect and much larger.
A concave lens held close always makes the letter look erect and enlarged.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A flat transparent glass piece does not change the apparent size and shape the way a lens does; a nearby convex lens can enlarge, while a concave lens does not make the letter look erect and enlarged.

teacher.key_rationale: Flat glass leaves size and shape unchanged. Enlarged erect views belong to a nearby convex lens, not to flat glass or to a concave lens used that way.
